_note:
What a blind box can pull, and how often — keyed by the retail product code.

A random booster is one product holding several beys, and which one you get is not yours to choose. The Taiwan sheet lists what is inside (as sub-codes of the box's code), so the app can already say what a box contains; what it cannot say is how likely each pull is. That is what this file is for, and it is the only thing entitled to put a number on the odds.

Without an entry a box still works. `acquire.ts` falls back to dividing by the beys the sheet lists under that code and marks the result `estimated`, which the sheet renders as "3 of the 6 beys we know it holds — ratios aren't published" rather than as a percentage. That hedge is not decoration: the sheet is known to under-list some boxes, so the denominator is a floor, not a count. An entry here replaces that guess with a counted one.

Each entry needs a `source` — the retail or wiki page the contents were read from — for the same reason every other curated file here does: a claim nobody can check is not worth showing. Kelab Gasing Beyblade's shop is the usual source where it still carries the box; it has been members-only since 6 Aug 2026, so newer entries cite the Beyblade Wiki's product page instead.

`share` is a relative frequency, not a percentage: a pull's chance is its share over the sum of them, so an even box is all 1s and nothing needs to add up to 100. Takara Tomy publishes an inclusion rate for only a few boxes; where the ratios are genuinely unknown but the contents are counted, write the shares as 1s and set `assumedEven` — the sheet then says the count is ours and the evenness is an assumption. Do not quietly write 1s without that flag: it turns a guess into a claim.

`blade` is the sheet's own product id, so a pull's ratchet and bit are read from the catalogue row rather than restated here and left to drift. `extra` is for a pull carrying a loose part the blade row does not name.

Empty as shipped. Every box in the catalogue is currently served by the hedged fallback above, and each entry added here is one box that stops guessing — start with the ones KGB actually stocks, whose English labels are in public/data/stock.json.
